bio.name: Haohua Que
bio.intro: I'm a Ph.D. student in Mechanical Engineering at the University of Georgia, working with Handong Yao in the Mobility Lab.
bio.focus: I study how autonomous systems perceive, plan, and operate under real-world constraints. My work connects driving robustness, robot exploration, and efficient AI deployment.

education.degree: Bachelor's degree in Electronic Information and Technology

honors.title: Third Prize
honors.description: Team award with the joint Sirius team, as captain of Beijing Forestry University's Forest Wolves team.

experience.description: Research on end-to-end autonomous driving, visual planning, and robustness under camera degradation. Participates in TRAVELS and leads the UGA RAV literature-review site.
Led the robotics group for two years. Co-first author of SenseExpo, combining lightweight occupancy prediction, frontier exploration, and ROS integration.

experience.organization: Beijing Forestry University · Forest Wolves RoboMaster Team
experience.description: Contributed to computer vision and mechanical development for the 2022 engineering robot. In 2023, the team joined with Beijing Information Science and Technology University as Sirius.

researchAreas.title: Reliable autonomy
researchAreas.description: Understanding when perception and planning fail, and how autonomous driving responds to degraded visual input.

researchAreas.title: Robot exploration
researchAreas.description: Helping robots explore unknown spaces through predictive maps and coordination across a swarm.

researchAreas.title: Efficient AI
researchAreas.description: Connecting models and hardware for perception under limits on bandwidth, memory, power, and latency.
